summary: Mr. Harari explains the rules for determining when Parshat Nissabim, Vayelekh, and Haazinu are read during the period between Rosh Hashanah and Sukkot. He also discusses the different pronunciations of the Shabbat between Rosh Hashanah and Kippur, noting the customs regarding the terms Shabbat Shuva and Shabbat Teshuvah.
questions: How do we determine if Nissabim and Vayelekh are read together or separately?
What is the significance of the day of the week Rosh Hashanah falls on for the Torah reading schedule?
Why is Haazinu always the final Parasha before Sukkot?
What are the two ways to pronounce the Shabbat between Rosh Hashanah and Kippur?
